subject: Intermittent tokenization-induced latency — advisory, mitigations, and follow-up
messages:
From: Sara Hu <sara.hu@acme-corp.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, support@redwood.com
Cc: support@acme-corp.com
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 15:13:00 +0000
Subject: High tail latency on streaming chat since ~14:50 UTC

Hi Grace,

We're seeing an increase in streaming latency on our chat integration starting around 14:50 UTC. Chat responses are taking 6–12s to emit the first streamed token, and in a few cases the stream stalls entirely and the client falls back to a full response. This is impacting our live support flow.

Examples: session ids S-9247, S-9251 — both from EU customers but routed through your us-east shard per our config.

We rolled our client to switch to non-streaming fallback (stream=false) for the worst-hit flows as a temporary step, but that increases visible latency for our users and we need a better workaround.

Can you confirm if this is a known issue on your side and share any suggested mitigations we can apply from the client side? Also please advise on ETA for a fix.

Thanks,
Sara
Sara Hu
Technical Program Manager
Acme Corp

--
ACME logs attached (ids redacted).
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Sara Hu <sara.hu@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 15:35:00 +0000
Subject: Re: High tail latency on streaming chat since ~14:50 UTC

Hi Sara — thanks for flagging this and for the helpful session ids. We're looking into it now. Initial notes and immediate mitigations below: 

- Short-term (client-side, immediate):
  - Continue using stream=false for the highest-priority flows; reduces perceived stalling.
  - Set max_output_tokens to 256 (if feasible) to reduce per-request generation time.
  - If you can, enable client-side retry with a small exponential backoff for streaming start (start retries at 500ms).

- Short-term (Redwood):
  - We have scoped a rollback for a tokenizer-side change that appears correlated with increased CPU per token on certain sequences.
  - We'll also push a temporary routing rule to favor older tokenizer workers for affected shards while the patch rolls out.

I've attached a short checklist for your engineering team (hotfix-steps.txt) that walks through the client adjustments above. We'll follow up with a post-incident summary and timeline once we have a full RCA.

I'll loop in Vivek and Monica from our infra and runtime teams to provide a technical timeline.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Head of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 02 Dec 2026 08:12:00 +0000
Subject: Re: High tail latency on streaming chat since ~14:50 UTC

Grace / Monica — quick technical triage summary and suggested next actions (RFC):

What we observed (early timeline)
- 14:45–14:52 UTC: tokenization service deploy (v2.2.7 -> v2.3.0) that introduced an optimization for combined Unicode handling.
- 14:50–15:10 UTC: elevated CPU on tokenizer workers processing long unicode-heavy prompts; streaming chunk flush windows extended resulting in 2–10s extra latency before the first chunk.

Root cause hypothesis
- A code path in the new tokenizer change increases per-token CPU for sequences with alternating emoji and punctuation (common in some Acme test sessions). The runtime's streaming flusher is sensitive to per-token processing time which pushed tail latency above SLOs.

Immediate mitigations performed
- Rolled back tokenizer to v2.2.7 on affected us-east routing pool at 15:20 UTC.
- Forced a routing preference to older workers for 12 minutes to allow safer rollback.
- Restarted streaming frontends in the affected pool to clear stale KV cache entries at 15:24 UTC.

Observed impact after actions
- By 15:40 UTC most reported streams recovered; residual elevated p95 persisted for ~30 minutes as caches warmed and in-flight sessions drained.

Proposed follow-ups (action items)
- Patch v2.3.0 to remove the costly codepath and add micro-benchmarks for emoji/punctuation-heavy sequences. Owner: Connor O'Brien. ETA: 48 hours for patch, 72 hours for full verification.
- Add heuristic to streaming flusher to cap initial chunk wait at 250ms and emit partial tokens earlier when encountering backpressure. Owner: Monica. ETA: 5 business days for rollout.
- Share postmortem and timeline to the customer and update incident tracker. Owner: Grace.

I've attached a short timeline diff we collected from the shard (timeline-diff.log). Happy to jump on a call with Acme if they'd like a real-time walk-through.

— Vivek
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
Attachment: timeline-diff.log (text)
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Sara Hu <sara.hu@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 02 Dec 2026 16:00:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Intermittent tokenization-induced latency — advisory, mitigations, and follow-up

Hi Sara — quick update and next steps.

Summary of what happened
- We released a tokenizer change (v2.3.0) that, under certain unicode-heavy inputs, increased CPU time-per-token. That increased the time before the streaming flusher emitted the first chunk for some sessions.

What we did quickly
- Rolled back the tokenizer for affected routing pools within ~35 minutes of detection.
- Applied routing workarounds and restarted frontends to clear impacted in-memory state.
- Provided client-side mitigations (see checklist) to reduce user-visible impact while we corrected the server side.

What we're doing next
- Patch to v2.3.0 that removes the problematic code path and adds unit/micro-benchmarks (Connor, ETA 48h).
- Streaming flusher changes to cap initial chunk wait and emit partial output under backpressure (Monica, ETA 5 business days).
- Full postmortem with timeline and corrective actions will be published to the link below and I'll share the PDF when available.

Compensation and support
- We're crediting Acme's account for two days of impacted usage as a gesture of goodwill while we complete the RCA. I'll coordinate with your billing contact — please let me know who that is.

If you'd like, we can schedule a 30-minute technical review with our infra team (Vivek or Connor) tomorrow to go through the timeline and the proposed patch plan.

Thanks again for the quick heads-up and patience while we worked through this. Apologies for the disruption.

Best regards,
Grace O'Connor
Head of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
